title: Zooming in at 8x: six directions on one scene
question: Which direction should zooming in take -- A today, B today with the water's level drawn, C sub-cell material texture, D chamfered edges, E smoothing, F brightness noise? Pick one, or say what B, C or D got wrong.
context_md:
Same world, same crop, same 1:1 colours in every pane -- only what the 64 pixels of each cell do differs. A stone basin of water beside a tree on the soil surface, pinned at noon.

- **A today** -- nearest-neighbour: every cell one flat 8x8 square.
- **B level drawn** -- as A, but a part-full water cell shows its fill as a level *line* inside the block instead of being dimmed toward black (today the surface row draws as a dark line). Fires on 39 cells here.
- **C material texture** -- as B, plus each mass is drawn the way it looks at 1x: sub-grains of the material's own palette inside the block, bark strips on wood, leaf cells rounded toward air. Hard edges, no blur.
- **D chamfered edges** -- as B, plus the staircase on a diagonal is cut to a 45-degree edge from what the neighbouring cells *are* (never from colour). Lone leaf cells become octagons; the roots pick up small diamonds.
- **E smoothing** -- bilinear between cell centres, the first thing 'upsample it' suggests. Blurs the grain and the edges.
- **F brightness noise** -- as A with a per-pixel brightness jitter at 15%.

**My reading, which is the thing to check:** E loses exactly the crispness the zoom-out complaint was about; F adds nothing. B is free and strictly more information. C is the biggest change and the one that answers 'big sharp squares'. D fixes silhouettes but changes the pixel character of single cells.

Cost under each pane is the arm's own per-output-pixel work on this box, single-threaded, over a full 512x320 frame -- at 8x the frame has the same pixel count as at 1x, so none of these grows with zoom, and none defeats the settled-world render skip (all are pure functions of the cell and its neighbours).

items.label: B level drawn
items.caption: fill as a line, not a dimming
